immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: MultipartCrossAdapterTest.upload() reflects into DefaultRequest.bodyStream and calls MultipartParser.parse with its own settings, form limit and SpoolRegistry, so the TinyHttpd side never goes through req.parts()/req.file()/req.form(), BodyState, the app spool registry or onError. FR-MULTIPART-001 AC-1 requires T13-T16 (and the non-disconnect T17 cases) to run over both adapters through the framework with the same results.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-tinyhttpd/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/tinyhttpd/MultipartCrossAdapterTest.java: delete the reflection upload() helper and the stale 'later fragment' class comment; build the app with app.multipart(o -> o.tempDirectory(tmp)) and a handler that reads req.parts() (names and sizes) and req.form()/req.file(); run each case over InMemoryHttpAdapter and over a TinyHttpd socket and assert equal status, body and, for 400/413 cases (bad boundary, header line 8193, header total >16384, 64 MiB+1), the FR-APP-006 standard error body. Add a T13 (FR-MULTIPART-003 AC-4 body) and a T14/T15 case (spooled part, maxFileSize 413) to the cross-adapter set and cite FR-MULTIPART-001 AC-1.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: no test sends text parts of 1048576 / 1048577 / 2x600000 bytes and none measures heap for a 32 MiB upload; FR-MULTIPART-004 AC-5 and AC-2 are untested, so a regression dropping the text total or buffering spooled parts would pass.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: Add to NaruServe-api/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/MultipartSpoolingTest.java (or MultipartLimitsTest) app-level tests over the in-memory adapter: default formLimit, one text part of 1048576 bytes reaches req.form(name) and req.parts(); one of 1048577 bytes and two of 600000 bytes each answer 413 with the standard error body; a text part counts against maxParts/maxRequestSize but not maxFileSize (maxFileSize(1024) with a 2000-byte text part is accepted). Add a heap test (FR-MULTIPART-004 AC-2): System.gc() + MemoryMXBean used heap before, then a 32 MiB file upload with default memoryThreshold, handler measures after System.gc() while holding the UploadFile, assert growth < 8 MiB. Cite the AC ids in test names. Fix MultipartParser only if a test goes red.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: MultipartLimitsTest.assert413/parse call MultipartParser directly and only check HttpException.status(); FR-MULTIPART-002 AC-1 and FR-MULTIPART-001 AC-2/AC-4 require the standard error body through onError when an accessor reads the body.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/MultipartLimitsTest.java: add app-level tests (TestApp + InMemoryHttpAdapter) with an onError handler that records the HttpException and delegates to the default answer: maxFileSize(1024) 1025-byte file, maxRequestSize(4096) overflow, 21 parts, header line 8193, missing boundary / missing close delimiter; assert status 413/400, the FR-APP-006 standard error JSON body, that onError saw HttpException with that status, and that the handler's accessor call threw HttpException. Keep the existing parser-level tests.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: MultipartParser.params() drops every backslash in a quoted value, so a browser-sent filename a/b\c.txt (one raw backslash; HTML form encoding percent-encodes only '"', CR and LF) becomes a/bc.txt. FR-MULTIPART-004 AC-3/AC-4 name 'a/b\c.txt (one backslash)' and require filename() unchanged; the test hides it by doubling the backslash on the wire.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/MultipartParser.java params(): inside a quoted value treat a backslash as an escape only when the next char is '"' or a backslash (curl-style escaping), otherwise append the backslash literally. Test: MultipartSpoolingTest#sdsAc2_FR_MULTIPART_004_AC3_tempNamesNeverDeriveFromClientValues sends the name raw (drop the name.replace doubling) and asserts filename() equals a/b\c.txt; add a case sending filename="a\"b.txt" -> a"b.txt. This aligns the test input with the AC, it does not weaken it.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: Dispatcher registers req.releaseUploads() in res.onDone, which fires when a non-streaming response completes even while the handler still runs, so res.send("queued"); f.save(dest) throws IllegalStateException. docs/api/multipart.md tells users to save() inside the handler; 'request ended' (D-252/D-254) is not defined as response completion in the SRS, and respond-then-process is a common Express/multer pattern.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/Dispatcher.java: release uploads when both the response is done (onDone, complete or abort) and the handler chain has returned (dispatch finally path), whichever comes last, e.g. an AtomicInteger countdown of 2 shared by onDone and the post-handler finally; the AFTER_ON_STOP participant stays the backstop. Update docs/api/multipart.md (임시 파일 정리) to say the request ends once the handler has returned and the response has finished. Tests: a handler doing res.status(202).send("queued"); f.save(dest) succeeds for a spooled part and tempDirectory is empty afterwards; existing FR-MULTIPART-005 AC-4 and FR-MULTIPART-006 AC-1/AC-4 tests stay green.

immediate_fix.rationale: Cheap real bug, verified: DefaultResponse.answerFile sets Content-Disposition before FileResponder.respond, which can throw FileNotFoundException/IOException; a user onError answering res.status(404).json(...) keeps the attachment header, so the error JSON downloads as a file.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/DefaultResponse.java answerFile: in the FileNotFoundException/IOException catch blocks remove the Content-Disposition header (response not started) before throwing HttpException. Test: res.download(missingFile, "x.pdf") with an onError answering res.status(404).json(...) has no Content-Disposition header.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: DefaultUploadFile.save() opens new FileOutputStream(destination) (truncating) before transferTo -> inputStream() throws IllegalStateException, so a second save(dest), or save after the request ended, wipes the file the first save wrote. Data loss; FR-MULTIPART-005 AC-4/AC-5 require only the throw.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/DefaultUploadFile.java save(): open the content InputStream first (try (InputStream in = inputStream(); OutputStream out = new FileOutputStream(destination)) { copy }) so IllegalStateException is thrown before the destination is opened, then close(). Test in DefaultUploadFileTest: pre-fill dest with known bytes; a second save(dest) and save after release throw IllegalStateException and dest still holds the first save's bytes, for in-memory and spooled parts.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: StaticHandler.wouldServeGet and the directory-301 branch of serveFrom use File.isFile()/isDirectory(), which follow symlinks, so a refused or outside-pointing symlink gets 405 Allow: GET, HEAD (or 301) while GET gets 404. FR-STATIC-002 AC-5 limits 405 to paths a GET would serve; it also leaks existence of refused links.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/StaticHandler.java: in wouldServeGet and before the 301 in serveFrom apply the mount resolver's canonical-containment + link check (FileResourceResolver check for files; listable() or the same check for directories) and treat a refused path as not served. Tests in StaticMethodTest: POST to a symlink file inside the root (allowSymlinks false) and to a symlink pointing outside -> 404; GET /linkdir (symlinked directory, no slash) -> 404, not 301.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: TinyHttpdFeatures.sendFile calls ex.commit before new RandomAccessFile(file, "r"); a missing file passes the range guard (length 0) and an unreadable one throws after commit, leaving a started response with Content-Length and no body instead of an unstarted response (FR-ENGINE-010, the restated FR-ENGINE-001 AC-2).
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-tinyhttpd/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/tinyhttpd/TinyHttpdFeatures.java sendFile: open the RandomAccessFile and seek(offset) first, then call ex.commit(...) inside the try-with-resources. Socket test (pattern of badOffsetOrLengthIsRefusedBeforeTheResponseStarts): sendFile on a missing file throws FileNotFoundException and the handler can still answer, response not started.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: StaticMount.freeze() keeps the same mutable DefaultStaticOptions the configurer received, so a retained reference can mutate its lists/maps after listen() while workers iterate them, bypassing the FR-APP-002 NEW-state guard.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/DefaultStaticOptions.java: add copy() returning a frozen instance with unmodifiable copies of spaExcludes, cachePatterns and mimes and copied scalar fields, whose setters throw IllegalStateException; StaticMount.freeze() passes options.copy(). Test: keep the configurer's StaticOptions reference, after listen() call o.index("x.html") / o.spaExclude("/x") and assert serving is unchanged (and the frozen copy refuses mutation).

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: StaticPath.check refuses decoded '/' and NUL but not a backslash; on a Windows JVM (supported Java 8+ target) /a%5C..%5C.env resolves to root\.env, and with allowSymlinks(true) bypasses the hidden-path 404 of FR-STATIC-005 AC-2. Cheap security hardening.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/StaticPath.java check(): treat a decoded segment containing a backslash like '/' and return 400 on every platform. Test in StaticTraversalTest: /a%5C..%5C.env and /a%5Cb.txt -> 400; update the traversal note in docs/api/static.md if it lists the refused characters.

immediate_fix.rationale: Verified: no test cites FR-STATIC-011 AC-5 (only AC-1..AC-4 are cited); the AC explicitly requires a test observing open/length/etag/modified on the built-in resolver for static mounts, res.file and res.download.
immediate_fix.fix_hypothesis: Add a test (in the internal test package, or via a package-private factory seam on FileResourceResolver) that installs a recording subclass/wrapper of the built-in FileResourceResolver and asserts open, length, etag and modified are each called for a static mount GET, res.file and res.download; name it sdsAc5_FR_STATIC_011_AC5_*. Production change limited to the package-private seam if needed.
